criteria.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-context (run `cargo test -p athena-context`) renders the reader brief and asserts its Reading rules section contains a rule requiring, for each reused existing struct field, CLI argument, record key or config key, a `Field meaning:` assumption quoting the documented meaning with a crates/ path:line and why it matches, or a new field when it does not. The test fails on the code before the change.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: `the_reader_brief_requires_a_field_meaning_assumption_for_a_reused_field ... ok`. The test renders `reader_brief(&reader_inputs(&reading()))` and cuts out the Reading rules section. It finds the bullet that contains `Field meaning:` in backticks, checks it equals a READING_RULES entry, and asserts the phrases CLI argument, record key, config key, documented meaning, crates/, path:line, why it fits, live athena.toml value, new field and quote. The base READING_RULES has no such line, so the `expect` fails there. Athena's fails-without run exited 101, though as a compile failure caused by the planner constant in the same test module.

criteria.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-context (`cargo test -p athena-context`) asserts the planner prompt/brief carries the same instruction, so a plan that reuses a field must quote its documented meaning and check the live athena.toml value; it fails before the change.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: `the_planner_brief_requires_a_reused_field_to_quote_its_meaning_and_check_the_live_config ... ok`. The test asserts the rendered `## Report` holds FIELD_MEANING_RULE exactly once and after REAL_RECORDS_RULE. It checks for the phrases struct field, CLI argument, record key, config key, documented meaning, crates/, path:line, live athena.toml value, each role and new field. It also checks the rule names no `via`, `hard_producer` or `restart`. Athena's fails-without run exited 101 (FIELD_MEANING_RULE is missing on the base).

criteria.criterion: The new rule is generic (any field, CLI argument, record key or config key), not specific to restart `via` or `hard_producer_*`; the diff of crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs shows it added to the Reading rules list marked `(prose only)`.
criteria.evidence: The diff of reader.rs changes `[&str; 12]` to `[&str; 13]` and adds one element: "Reused field, CLI argument, record key or config key needs `Field meaning:` assumption: ... or a new field (prose only)." It names no field from either job. The extended `the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line` passes. It asserts the line ends with `(prose only).`, contains no `via` token, no restart, no hard_producer and no `check_`, and is at most 220 bytes.

summary: The change finds the root cause where it starts. Neither the reader brief nor the planner brief told the stage to read a reused field's documented meaning before mapping a requirement onto it, so both briefs now carry that rule. It adds one generic `(prose only)` line to READING_RULES (rendered at reader.rs:572-573) and one new constant, FIELD_MEANING_RULE, which is printed in the planner brief's Report section. It adds no refusal check, and nothing in crates/athena-core changes. Athena's replay found 0 of 50 past accepted readings newly refused. I ran the two new tests and the extended rule-line test, and all pass. Athena's fails-without runs showed the new tests fail on the base code. That failure was a compile failure. The reader test also cannot pass on the base, because the base has no `Field meaning:` line. The CHANGELOG entry and the new D180 entry in docs/decisions.md both name the root cause and cite both jobs, and D180 has a Provenance bullet. No prompt file changed, so no token budget moves. CI recorded fmt, clippy and test as passing. Two minor findings: crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs changed but is not an expected deliverable (it was planned, and holds the required tests), and the critic was not given the rule.
